concerns.text: Task T058 (pre‑flight URL verification) is placed **after** the ingestion tasks (T012a/T012b) that actually download the datasets. The pre‑flight check must run **before** any download to satisfy the producer‑before‑consumer ordering rule.

Task T055 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it mutates `data/processed/unified_data.csv` by hashing user IDs. Running it in parallel with any other task that reads or writes the same file would cause a race condition, violating the parallel‑safety guarantee.

Task T056 is also marked `[P]` yet it modifies the same `data/processed/unified_data.csv` (grouping rare countries). Parallel execution with other tasks that access this file would lead to nondeterministic state.
Task T059 sets a global random seed. If executed in parallel with other tasks that rely on randomness, the seed could be overwritten, breaking reproducibility. Therefore `[P]` is inappropriate.
Task T061 is a unit test that reads `data/processed/unified_data.csv`. Marking it `[P]` suggests it can run concurrently with tasks that write the same file, which is unsafe.
Task T062 tests country grouping on the same processed data file; parallel execution with the grouping task (T056) would cause a race condition.
Task T063 checks overlap size on the real dataset. If run in parallel with the ingestion tasks (T012a/T012b) it may read incomplete data, violating the ordering rule.
Task T064 simulates a pipeline abort on missing data and depends on the download logic. Running it in parallel with the actual download tasks could mask the intended failure mode.
